opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Sloan (employee ID E043) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E043.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Karen Sloan (E043) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee whose role owns the Payroll system, admin is permitted under policy.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E043 (Karen Sloan) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as HR noted. Contractors never get admin. Basic training means write is not permitted; max is read. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: Karen Sloan (E043) requested admin access to Payroll. The Security note, which verified employment type and security training in its own database, records her as a contractor with basic security training, and explicitly contradicts the HR note's full-time claim. Under policy, contractors may never have admin; with basic training the maximum is read. Since the requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (read), I grant the maximum: read.
